checks: Verified original §4, equations (12)–(15). The set of equal-base continuous differences equals the slice of C−C and is already compact, convex and symmetric, so no additional convex hull is needed. Positive fibers make R and S_* strictly positive; the enclosing-ball bound makes section suprema finite, also with counting measure.

For a regular stress, the cap-plus-section and contact measures are nonnegative, supported in C, and by the mass/base equations have common mass W_i and base centroid. Their probability barycenters lie at the same real base and their continuous difference is (Ψ_i/W_i)u_i by the Euler equation. This gives the directional inclusion and radius bound; W_i=0 implies c_i=0 and zero hinge.
Summing Ψ_i≤RW_i, using S_i≤S_*, c_i≤τM and nonnegative r_i, gives v≤R(NτM−S_*v′/M). Multiplying by M/(RS_*) gives A=M/(RS_*) and B=NM²/S_* with the stated signs.

The integrating factor gives the derivative bound on each regular interval; limits through the finitely many exceptional points add only downward jumps because v is nonincreasing and right-continuous. The bound therefore holds on every stated compact interval including exceptional endpoints.
